19: void bk7258_led_initialize(void)
20: {
21:   if (!g_led_initialized)

29: void board_autoled_on(int led)
30: {
31:   switch (led)
32:     {
33:       case LED_ASSERTION:
34:       case LED_PANIC:
35:         g_red_states |= 1u << led;
36:         bk7258_gpio_write(BOARD_LED_RED_GPIO, true);
37:         break;
38: 
39:       case LED_INIRQ:
40:       case LED_SIGNAL:
41:       case LED_IDLE:
42:       case LED_HEAPALLOCATE:
43:       case LED_IRQSENABLED:
44:       case LED_STACKCREATED:
45:         g_green_states |= 1u << led;
46:         bk7258_gpio_write(BOARD_LED_GREEN_GPIO, true);
47:         break;
48: 
49:       default:
50:         break;
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: void board_autoled_off(int led)
55: {
56:   switch (led)
57:     {
58:       case LED_ASSERTION:
59:         g_red_states &= ~(1u << led);
60:         if (g_red_states == 0)
61:           {
62:             bk7258_gpio_write(BOARD_LED_RED_GPIO, false);
63:           }
64:         break;
65: 
66:       case LED_INIRQ:
67:       case LED_SIGNAL:
68:       case LED_IDLE:
69:       case LED_HEAPALLOCATE:
70:       case LED_IRQSENABLED:
71:       case LED_STACKCREATED:
72:         g_green_states &= ~(1u << led);
73:         if (g_green_states == 0)
74:           {
75:             bk7258_gpio_write(BOARD_LED_GREEN_GPIO, false);
76:           }
77:         break;
78: 
79:       case LED_PANIC:
80:         /* Keep the red LED latched until reset after a panic. */
81:       default:

11:  * 4 data bytes per command (see bk7258_qspi.h), which hard-blocks porting

14:  *   0xF1(6) 0xF3(6), plus the special 0x00/data_len=0xFF delay marker

17:  * 0x71, 0x91, 0x34) all fit within the 4-byte limit and were dropped in

19:  * documents them as gamma/porch/timing fine-tuning registers that are not

21:  * independently confirmed against the GC9D01 datasheet.  If the panel

44:  *      dual-screen reference config in BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md);
45:  *      the schematic shows GPIO_6 floating (unconnected) on this board,
46:  *      the real LCD_RST net is GPIO45.

50:  * against gpio_map.h's pinmux function tables.

65:  * (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf) after this driver's original QSPI0/GPIO6
66:  * assumption (ported from BTdocs/DualScreenAVIPlayer.md's lcd0 config,
67:  * a *different* board's dual-screen reference layout) caused the very
68:  * first init command (0xFE) to time out -- the panel was never wired to
69:  * the pins this driver was toggling.  The schematic (sheet 2/6 main chip
70:  * pin table) shows GPIO_6 net-labelled nothing at all on this board
71:  * (floating, no connection); the actual LCD_RST net is wired to chip pin
72:  * 65 = P45 = GPIO45 (same sheet's pin table row "P45/0CSN/B5/D2/2LRCK"),
73:  * confirmed again on sheet 5/6's CN5 single-screen connector pin 13
74:  * (labelled LCD_RST). See bk7258_qspi.c's file header for the QSPI0->
75:  * QSPI1 correction that was diagnosed alongside this one (both changes
76:  * were needed to get past the same "cmd 0xFE timed out" symptom). */

79: /* Post-Sleep-Out settle delay before Display On, per upstream
80:  * gc9d01_init_cmds entry {0x00, {0x78}, 0xFF} (0x78 = 120 decimal ms). */

96:   { 0xEF, { 0x00 }, 0 },
97:   { 0x80, { 0xFF }, 1 },

99:   { 0x82, { 0xFF }, 1 },
100:   { 0x83, { 0xFF }, 1 },

102:   { 0x85, { 0xFF }, 1 },
103:   { 0x86, { 0xFF }, 1 },
104:   { 0x87, { 0xFF }, 1 },
105:   { 0x88, { 0xFF }, 1 },
106:   { 0x89, { 0xFF }, 1 },
107:   { 0x8A, { 0xFF }, 1 },
108:   { 0x8B, { 0xFF }, 1 },
109:   { 0x8C, { 0xFF }, 1 },
110:   { 0x8D, { 0xFF }, 1 },

118:   { 0x7E, { 0x30 }, 1 },

120:   { 0xC4, { 0x18 }, 1 },
121:   { 0xC9, { 0x3C }, 1 },
122:   { 0x36, { 0x00 }, 1 },
123:   { 0x11, { 0x00 }, 0 }, /* Sleep Out */
124: };

126: #define GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT \
127:   (sizeof(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out) / \
128:    sizeof(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[0]))

133: /****************************************************************************
134:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset
135:  *
136:  * Description:
137:  *   Drive the GC9D01 RESET pin through a high-low-high pulse to force a
138:  *   hardware reset.  Timing: the 10ms pre/post pulse widths are a
139:  *   conservative margin (GC9D01 reset pulse width requirements are
140:  *   typically in the microsecond range; 10ms has no specific datasheet
141:  *   citation but costs nothing at bring-up time).  The final 120ms
142:  *   post-reset settle delay before issuing any command matches the
143:  *   reset-to-ready delay used across every other panel driver in the same
144:  *   bk_avdk_smp codebase (ap/components/bk_peripheral/src/lcd/rgb and .../mcu
145:  *   uniformly use rtos_delay_milliseconds(120) after hardware reset, e.g.
146:  *   lcd_st7701s.c:48, lcd_nt35512.c:859, lcd_st7789v.c:167), i.e. 120ms is
147:  *   the de-facto standard settle time for this class of display driver IC
148:  *   and is not GC9D01-specific tuning.
149:  *
150:  ****************************************************************************/
151: 
152: static void bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset(void)
153: {
154:   bk7258_gpio_output(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, true);
155:   up_udelay(10000);
156:   bk7258_gpio_write(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, false);
157:   up_udelay(10000);
158:   bk7258_gpio_write(GC9D01_RESET_PIN, true);
159:   up_udelay(120000);
160: }

162: /****************************************************************************
163:  * Name: bk7258_gc9d01_test
164:  *
165:  * Description:
166:  *   Bring-up smoke test for the GC9D01 panel: hardware reset, QSPI0 init,
167:  *   then send the full init command sequence (pre-Sleep-Out commands,
168:  *   Sleep Out, 120ms settle delay, Display On).  There is no Read ID
169:  *   command in the upstream init table (verified: the only "0x04" bytes
170:  *   found in lcd_spi_gc9d01.c are payload data, not an RDID opcode), so
171:  *   this test cannot verify success by reading back a panel ID.  Success
172:  *   criterion is therefore "the full init sequence is sent without the
173:  *   call hanging or crashing", not a register readback match.
174:  *
175:  ****************************************************************************/
176: 
177: int bk7258_gc9d01_test(int argc, char **argv)
178: {
179:   size_t i;
180: 
181:   printf("gc9d01: hardware reset\n");
182:   bk7258_gc9d01_hw_reset();
183: 
184:   printf("gc9d01: qspi0 init\n");
185:   bk7258_qspi0_init();
186: 
187:   printf("gc9d01: sending %u init commands (through sleep out)\n",
188:          (unsigned int)GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT);
189:   for (i = 0; i < GC9D01_PRE_SLEEP_OUT_CMD_COUNT; i++)
190:     {
191:       if (!bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].cmd,
192:                                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].data,
193:                                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].data_len))
194:         {
195:           printf("gc9d01: qspi0 timed out waiting for cmd 0x%02x "
196:                  "(index %u) to complete, aborting init sequence\n",
197:                  g_gc9d01_init_cmds_pre_sleep_out[i].cmd, (unsigned int)i);
198:           return -1;
199:         }
200:     }
201: 
202:   printf("gc9d01: sleep-out settle delay (%u ms)\n",
203:          GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS);
204:   up_udelay(GC9D01_SLEEP_OUT_DELAY_MS * 1000u);
205: 
206:   printf("gc9d01: display on\n");
207:   if (!bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(g_gc9d01_display_on.cmd,
208:                               g_gc9d01_display_on.data,
209:                               g_gc9d01_display_on.data_len))
210:     {
211:       printf("gc9d01: qspi0 timed out waiting for display-on cmd to "
212:              "complete\n");
213:       return -1;
214:     }
215: 
216:   printf("gc9d01: init sequence completed without hang\n");
217:   return 0;

149: bk7258_start(void)
150: {
151:   const uint8_t *src;
152:   uint8_t *dest;
153: 
154:   /* Configure the FPU before code compiled for the hard-float ABI can use
155:    * it.  arm_fpuconfig() does not depend on BSS-backed synchronization.
156:    */
157: 
158:   arm_fpuconfig();
159:   UP_DSB();
160:   UP_ISB();
161:   for (src = _eronly, dest = _sdata; dest < _edata; )
162:     {
163:       *dest++ = *src++;
164:     }
165: 
166:   for (dest = _sbss; dest < _ebss; )
167:     {
168:       *dest++ = 0;
169:     }
170: 
171:   for (src = __ram_vectors_load, dest = __ram_vectors_start;
172:        dest < __ram_vectors_end; )
173:     {
174:       *dest++ = *src++;
175:     }

190:     }

42: static int bk7258_motor_button_worker(int argc, char **argv)
43: {
44:   struct pwm_info_s info =
45:   {
46:     .frequency = BK7258_MOTOR_FREQUENCY,
47:     .duty = BK7258_MOTOR_DUTY,
48:   };
49:   bool candidate = false;
50:   bool pressed = false;
51:   unsigned int samples = 0;
52:   int ret;
53:   int fd = -1;
54:   clock_t request_start;
55: 
56:   (void)argc;
57:   (void)argv;
58:   request_start = clock_systime_ticks();
59:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(BK7258_PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD,
60:                                 BK7258_PM_CLK_ID_PWM_1,
61:                                 BK7258_PM_CLK_POWER_UP, 0);
62:   if (ret < 0)
63:     {
64:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM clock request failed: %d\n", ret);
65:       goto ready;
66:     }
67: 
68:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(200);
69:   syslog(LOG_INFO, "power-key motor: PWM clock transport wait=%d elapsed=%lu ms\n",
70:          ret, (unsigned long)TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - request_start));
71:   if (ret < 0)
72:     {
73:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM clock ACK failed: %d\n", ret);
74:       goto ready;
75:     }
76: 
77:   nxsig_usleep(20000);
78:   fd = open("/dev/pwm0", O_RDWR);
79:   if (fd < 0)
80:     {
81:       ret = -errno;
82:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: open pwm0 failed: %d\n", ret);
83:       goto ready;
84:     }
85: 
86:   if (ioctl(fd, PWMIOC_SETCHARACTERISTICS,
87:             (unsigned long)(uintptr_t)&info) < 0)
88:     {
89:       ret = -errno;
90:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: set PWM characteristics failed: %d\n",
91:              ret);
92:       close(fd);
93:       goto ready;
94:     }
95: 
96:   ret = OK;
97: 
98: ready:
99:   g_motor_worker_result = ret;
100:   nxsem_post(&g_motor_ready_sem);
101:   if (ret < 0)
102:     {
103:       return ret;
104:     }
105: 
106:   printf("power-key motor worker ready, PWM parameters applied\n");
107: 
108:   for (;;)
109:     {
110:       bool sample = (board_buttons() & BUTTON_POWER_BIT) != 0;
111: 
112:       if (sample != candidate)
113:         {
114:           candidate = sample;
115:           samples = 1;
116:         }
117:       else if (samples < BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT)
118:         {
119:           samples++;
120:         }
121: 
122:       if (samples == BK7258_KEY_DEBOUNCE_COUNT && pressed != candidate)
123:         {
124:           int cmd = candidate ? PWMIOC_START : PWMIOC_STOP;
125:           clock_t edge_start = clock_systime_ticks();
126: 
127:           if (ioctl(fd, cmd, 0) < 0)
128:             {
129:               syslog(LOG_ERR, "power-key motor: PWM cmd=%d failed: %d\n",
130:                      cmd, -errno);
131:               close(fd);
132:               return -errno;
133:             }
134: 
135:           pressed = candidate;
136:           syslog(LOG_INFO,
137:                  "power-key motor: button=%u, pwm cmd=%d applied elapsed=%lu ms\n",
138:                  candidate, cmd,
139:                  (unsigned long)TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - edge_start));
140:         }

142:       nxsig_usleep(BK7258_KEY_POLL_US);
143:     }

120:   if (!priv->setup || info == NULL || info->frequency == 0)
121:     {

123:     }

125:   period = BK7258_PWM_CLOCK_HZ / info->frequency;
126:   if (period < 2 || period > UINT32_MAX)

129:     }

132:   if (duty > period)

135:     }

138:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2, 0);

143:   putreg32((uint32_t)(period - duty), BK7258_PWM_CCR4);
144:   putreg32((uint32_t)period, BK7258_PWM_CCR5);
145:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CCMR,
146:               BK7258_PWM_CCMR_TIM2CCM | BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_MASK,
147:               BK7258_PWM_CCMR_CH4E |
148:               (duty == 0 ? BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_LOW :
149:                duty == period ? BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_HIGH :
150:                BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_TOGGLE));
151:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_EDTR, 0, BK7258_PWM_EDTR_UG2);
152:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, 0, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2);

151: {
152:   /* Enable the QSPI1 *module* clock gate first, matching
153:    * qspi_id_init_common()'s documented call order ("1. set clock, 2. set
154:    * gpio as qspi, 3. enable interrupt") in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
155:    * ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c.  Without this bit, register
156:    * writes to the QSPI1 block are accepted (no bus fault) but the
157:    * controller's internal command state machine has no clock to run on,
158:    * so cmd_start_done never asserts -- see
159:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
160:    * the register-map citation and the I2C1 precedent this is modeled
161:    * after. */

163:

165:    * controller; see file header comment for why this is required and why

167:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CLK_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
168:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CSN_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);

175: 
176: - `ram_regions.csv`
177: - AP/CP `config`
178: - Kconfig 默认值
179: - 分区生成脚本
180: - SoC 链接脚本
181: 
182: 原因是顶层 `partitions/ram_regions.h` 可以先更新，而 AP/CP CMake 构建目录中的
183: `armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv`、生成头和预处理链接脚本仍可能保留旧值。
184: 这会形成顶层 16 MiB、核内仍 8 MiB 的不一致产物。
185: 
186: 先构建 OpenVela AP，并将输入放到 Armino 工作树：
187: 
188: ```bash
189: cd ~/vela_competition/contest
190: ./build.sh \
191:   vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh \
192:   -e -Werror --cmake -j8
193: 
194: cp \
195:   cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin \
196:   ~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
197: ```
198: 
199: 然后执行项目级 clean 和容器内完整构建：
200: 
201: ```bash
202: cd ~/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp
203: make -C projects/app_ab clean
204: 
205: podman run --rm \
206:   --userns=keep-id \
207:   -v "$PWD:/armino" \
208:   -w /armino \
209:   -e EXTRA_CFLAGS=-Werror \
210:   localhost/bekencorp/armino-idk:1.5 \
211:   make -C projects/app_ab bk7258 \
212:   SDK_DIR=/armino \
213:   EXTERNAL_AP_BIN=/armino/build/openvela-ap.bin
214: ```
215: 
216: `make -C projects/app_ab clean`只删除`projects/app_ab/build`，不会删除
217: `build/openvela-ap.bin`。仅安装 Podman 时不要使用内部调用 Docker 的`dbuild.sh`。
218: 
219: CP 构建后先对生成配置做门禁，再恢复最小输入 fragment：
220: 
221: ```bash
222: generated=projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/config/sdkconfig.h
223: grep -q '^#define CONFIG_OPENVELA_AP_CPU1_480M 1$' "$generated"
224: grep -q '^#define CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_AP_IPV4 1$' "$generated"
225: grep -q '^#define CONFIG_GPIO_DEFAULT_SET_SUPPORT 1$' "$generated"
226: 
227: mirror=../contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp
228: cp "$mirror/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config" \
229:   projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config
230: cmp -s "$mirror/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config" \
231:   projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config
232: ```
233: 
234: 权威 config 经确认是 7 行最小种子（首个空行加 6 行配置，包含单核 CPU1 480 MHz
235: 频率项和显式关闭 SARADC mailbox），完整生成配置只存在于 build 目录，不回写比赛仓。
236: 
237: ## 4. 构建验收
238: 
239: 以下文件必须都反映同一份 16 MiB 布局：
240: 
241: ```text
242: projects/app_ab/partitions/bk7258/ram_regions.csv
243: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/partitions/ram_regions.h
244: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv
245: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258_ap/armino/partitions/_build/ram_regions.csv
246: projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/bk7258/bk7258_out.ld

248: ```
249: 
250: 关键值应为：
251: 
252: ```text
253: CONFIG_PSRAM_CAPACITY          0x01000000
254: CP_PSRAM_HEAP                 0x60700000 + 0x00020000
255: AP_PSRAM_HEAP                 0x60720000 + 0x002e0000
256: AP_PSRAM_SECTION              0x60a00000 + 0x00600000
257: PSRAM 最终边界                0x61000000
258: ```

261:

263: sha256sum \
264:   ~/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin \

29: 
30: LED 初始化位于：

33: board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_boot.c
34: ```

46: ```
47: 
48: 初始化时将 GPIO40 和 GPIO41 配置为普通输出，并设置为低电平，避免 LED 在
49: NuttX 内核初始化前处于不确定状态。
50: 
51: ## 4. 内核状态映射
52: 
53: ### 绿色 LED GPIO41
54: 
55: 以下状态会点亮绿灯：
56: 
57: ```text
58: LED_INIRQ
59: LED_SIGNAL
60: LED_IDLE
61: LED_HEAPALLOCATE
62: LED_IRQSENABLED
63: LED_STACKCREATED
64: ```
65: 
66: 最主要的运行时状态是 `LED_INIRQ`：
67: 
68: ```text
69: 进入中断 -> board_autoled_on(LED_INIRQ)  -> 绿灯亮
70: 退出中断 -> board_autoled_off(LED_INIRQ) -> 绿灯灭
71: ```
72: 
73: 因此 UART、SysTick、Mailbox、定时器等中断频繁发生时，绿灯会快速闪烁。
74: 当闪烁频率较高时，肉眼可能观察为低亮度常亮或亮度变化，这不是 PWM。
75: 
76: ### 红色 LED GPIO40
77: 
78: 以下状态会点亮红灯：
79: 
80: ```text
81: LED_ASSERTION
82: LED_PANIC
83: ```
84: 
85: `LED_ASSERTION` 结束后可以关闭红灯。`LED_PANIC` 不响应关闭操作，红灯会保持
86: 点亮直到系统复位，用于保留 Panic 状态。
87: 
88: ## 5. 状态位图
89: 
90: 为了避免多个内核状态相互覆盖，驱动分别维护两个状态位图：
91: 
92: ```c
93: static volatile uint32_t g_green_states;
94: static volatile uint32_t g_red_states;
95: ```
96: 
97: 点亮某个状态时设置对应 bit，关闭某个状态时清除对应 bit。只有当对应位图
98: 完全为零时，才会真正关闭 LED。
99: 
100: 例如：
101: 
102: ```text
103: LED_STACKCREATED on
104: LED_IRQSENABLED on
105: LED_IRQSENABLED off
106: ```
107: 
108: 此时 `LED_STACKCREATED` 仍然有效，所以绿灯继续保持点亮，不会被提前关闭。

3:  *
4:  * Interrupt-driven hardware I2C1 master driver.
5:  *
6:  * This replaces the earlier software-simulated (bit-banged) I2C driver
7:  * (bk7258_i2c_sim.c/.h) for GC2145 camera register access.  The switch
8:  * was forced by the board schematic (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf, sheet
9:  * 4/6 "DVP/SENSOR/NAND/MOTOR/KEY"), which shows GC2145's SCL/SDA wired to
10:  * the chip's *hardware* I2C1 peripheral (network labels IIC1_SCL/
11:  * IIC1_SDA, with 4.7K pull-ups to VDDGPIO) -- not to a pair of plain
12:  * GPIOs that firmware could bit-bang arbitrarily.  The previous driver's
13:  * choice of GPIO0/GPIO1 for bit-banging was based on a reference
14:  * project's default config (bk_avdk_smp dvp_example) that does not match
15:  * this board: GPIO0/GPIO1 are actually wired to UART1_TXD/UART1_RXD here
16:  * (schematic sheet 2/6 pin table), which explains why every prior
17:  * hardware bring-up attempt saw the GC2145 never ACK the first I2C byte
18:  * -- the bit-banged signal was toggling the wrong physical pins.
19:  *
20:  * The real IIC1_SCL/IIC1_SDA nets are routed by the chip's pinmux to
21:  * GPIO42/GPIO43 (bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h
22:  * GPIO_I2C1_MAP_TABLE's second entry, BIT64(42)|BIT64(43); the first
23:  * entry, GPIO0/GPIO1, is I2C1's *other* selectable pin group used by a
24:  * different board, not this one).  This driver hard-codes GPIO42/43 as
25:  * this board's only wiring; it is not a general-purpose pinmux-selectable
26:  * I2C1 driver.
27:  *
28:  * Architecture: this is a from-scratch reimplementation of the interrupt
29:  * + semaphore master state machine in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
30:  * ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c (i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl(),
31:  * i2c_master_isr_common(), i2c1_isr_common()), adapted to NuttX's
32:  * irq_attach()/up_enable_irq()/nxsem_wait() primitives in place of
33:  * Beken RTOS's bk_int_isr_register()/rtos_get_semaphore().  Only the
34:  * master-write path is implemented (I2C_MASTER_WRITE state sequence:
35:  * START -> TX_DEV_ADDR -> TX_MEM_ADDR -> TX_DATA -> STOP); master-read,
36:  * slave mode, 10-bit addressing, and low-power-sleep register
37:  * backup/restore are intentionally omitted, since GC2145 bring-up (585 +
38:  * 40 register writes, all 8-bit register address / 8-bit data, no
39:  * readback) is this driver's only consumer.
40:  */

10: #include <stdint.h>
11: 
12: /* Minimal YUV_BUF driver: YUV direct-capture mode only (ctrl.yuv_mode=1,
13:  * ctrl.h264_mode=0), no JPEG/H264 hardware encoder path.
14:  *
15:  * Ping-pong semantics (per bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
16:  * ap/components/bk_dvp/src/bk_dvp.c yuv_sm0_line_done()/
17:  * yuv_sm1_line_done()): the hardware's PSRAM line buffer is two adjacent
18:  * regions of bk7258_yuv_buf_get_line_batch_bytes() bytes each, both
19:  * starting at bk7258_yuv_buf_get_line_buf_addr().  SM0_WR fires when the
20:  * *first* region (offset 0) has just been filled with the next 8 lines;
21:  * SM1_WR fires when the *second* region (offset
22:  * +line_batch_bytes) has been filled.  The hardware keeps alternating
23:  * between the two regions on every successive batch of 8 lines,
24:  * regardless of whether software has finished draining the previous one
25:  * -- callers must copy out each region promptly (via DMA) before the
26:  * hardware writes the *next* occurrence of that same region, or the data
27:  * is silently overwritten.  This driver's callback signature exposes
28:  * which region (SM0 or SM1) fired so callers can compute the correct DMA
29:  * source address without needing to know the ping-pong length
30:  * themselves (see bk7258_yuv_buf_get_line_batch_bytes()).
31:  */
32: 
33: typedef enum bk7258_yuv_buf_bank_e
34: {
35:   BK7258_YUV_BUF_BANK_SM0 = 0,
36:   BK7258_YUV_BUF_BANK_SM1 = 1,
37: } bk7258_yuv_buf_bank_t;

- Enabled by [defconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:97).

- Supporting symbols are `CONFIG_BUILTIN=y`, `CONFIG_NSH_BUILTIN_APPS=y`, `CONFIG_TTY_SIGINT=y`, `CONFIG_TTY_SIGINT_CHAR=0x03`, and `CONFIG_SCHED_WAITPID=y`.
- The current CMake artifact confirms it was compiled and linked: [builtin_list.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/apps/builtin/builtin_list.h:7), `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/System.map`, and `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.map`.

Canonical build command, documented in [external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:186):

**Device Surface**

- `/dev/console`: mailbox-backed CP UART0 console.
- `/dev/ttyMB0`: second name for the same mailbox UART device. Registration is in [bk7258_serial.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:248). Symbols: `CONFIG_BK7258_MB_UART0_CONSOLE`, `CONFIG_BK7258_MBOX_V2`.
- `/dev/gpio0`: volume-up key, GPIO13, active-low but exposed as ASCII `1` when pressed.
- `/dev/gpio1`: power key, GPIO12, same pressed semantics.
- `/dev/gpio2`: volume-down key, GPIO8. Registration and inversion are in [bk7258_buttons.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_buttons.c:26). Symbols: `CONFIG_ARCH_BUTTONS`, `CONFIG_DEV_GPIO`.
- `/dev/pwm0`: PWM lower-half for vibration, GPIO9 PWM plus GPIO52 LDO. Registered in [bk7258_motor.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:147). Symbols: `CONFIG_PWM`, `CONFIG_BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR`. Excluded from the requested test.
- `/dev/video0`: V4L2 camera node registered in [bk7258_camera_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_camera_bringup.c:29). Excluded from the requested test.
- `wlan0`: Wi-Fi network interface, not a `/dev` node. Registered through `netdev_lower_register(..., NET_LL_IEEE80211)` in [bk7258_wifi.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_wifi.c:1890). Symbols: `CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI`, `CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_TX_SLOTS=8`, `CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI`, `CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI_CMDTOOL`.
- `/proc`: procfs mounted during bring-up under `CONFIG_FS_PROCFS`.

There is no `/dev/userleds`, `/dev/fb0`, `/dev/qspi*`, `/dev/i2c*`, `/dev/psram`, or `/dev/timer0`. SysTick is used directly as the architecture scheduler timer.

**Commands And APIs**

Current application commands are exactly `renew`, `nsh`, `sh`, `nxcamera`, `ping`, `wapi`, and `ctrlc_test`, as shown by the generated builtin table above. Relevant NSH-native commands include `help`, `ls`, `cat`, `ps`, `free`, `uptime`, `sleep`, `uname`, `ifconfig`, and `ifup`.

- GPIO API: `bk7258_gpio_input_pullup`, `bk7258_gpio_output`, `bk7258_gpio_write`, `bk7258_gpio_read`, `bk7258_gpio_set_function` in [bk7258_gpio.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_gpio.h:19).
- Buttons/LED API: `board_button_initialize`, `board_buttons`, `board_autoled_on/off`, `bk7258_led_initialize` in [board.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/include/board.h:40). LEDs are GPIO40 red and GPIO41 green.
- PSRAM API: initialization, allocation, media pools, `bk7258_psram_info`, and `bk7258_psram_dump` in [bk7258_psram.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_psram.h:61). Symbols: `CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM`, `CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_KEEP_POWERED`, `CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_SIZE=0x01000000`.
- LCD/QSPI API: `bk7258_qspi0_init`, `bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd`, `bk7258_qspi0_read_id` in [bk7258_qspi.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_qspi.h:19), plus `bk7258_gc9d01_test()` in [bk7258_gc9d01.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01.c:177). Despite the `qspi0` API name, this board drives hardware QSPI1 on GPIO2-5 and LCD reset on GPIO45.
- Mailbox/UART APIs, including link wait, diagnostics, heartbeat, and UART read/write, are declared in [bk7258_mbox.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:245).
- Wi-Fi’s public board API is `bk7258_wifi_initialize()` in [bk7258_wifi.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_wifi.h:8); user control goes through standard wireless ioctls and `wapi`.

I2C1, DMA, and YUV-buffer APIs exist, but are currently camera-specific and therefore excluded: [bk7258_i2c1.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_i2c1.h:48), [bk7258_dma.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_dma.h:27), and [bk7258_yuv_buf.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_yuv_buf.h:33).

**Practical Self-Test**

1. On CP, run `ap_console status`, then `ap_console open`.
2. Confirm boot output contains `mailbox UART0 link ready`, `button GPIOs configured, count=3`, `PSRAM online, base=0x60000000 size=0x01000000`, `heartbeat worker started`, and `board bring-up initialization completed`.
3. Run `ls /dev`, `ls /proc`, `uname -a`, `ps`, `free`, and `uptime`; run `sleep 2` followed by `uptime` to exercise SysTick scheduling.
4. Run `ctrlc_test`, wait several seconds, then press Ctrl-C. Require `ctrlc_test received SIGINT`. This tests mailbox UART RX/TX, `/dev/console`, TTY signal handling, scheduler wakeup, and the green `LED_SIGNAL` path.
5. Run `cat /dev/gpio0`, `cat /dev/gpio1`, and `cat /dev/gpio2` released; expect `0`. Hold volume-up while reading `/dev/gpio0`, and volume-down while reading `/dev/gpio2`; expect `1`.
6. Testing `/dev/gpio1` pressed will automatically start vibration after roughly 30 ms because `CONFIG_BK7258_POWER_KEY_MOTOR=y`. To exclude vibration strictly, only verify its released value in this firmware.
7. Observe GPIO41 green activity during interrupts and Ctrl-C delivery; GPIO40 red must remain off. There is no non-destructive shell command for explicitly driving either LED.
8. PSRAM’s boot path performs a bounded boundary read/write probe and initializes all heaps. A deeper test requires an app call to `bk7258_psram_malloc()`, write/read a pattern, check `bk7258_psram_contains()`, free it, then call `bk7258_psram_info()` or `bk7258_psram_dump()`.
9. LCD has no current NSH command and its automatic test call is commented out in [bk7258_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:121). Complete coverage requires invoking `bk7258_gc9d01_test(0, NULL)` from a diagnostic builtin. Expected result is `gc9d01: init sequence completed without hang`; this verifies reset and QSPI command completion, not pixels or panel ID.

**Wi-Fi Commands**

Run Wi-Fi separately so association or DHCP failures do not obscure the base peripheral test:

```text
ifup wlan0
wapi show wlan0
wapi country wlan0 CN
wapi mode wlan0 2
wapi scan wlan0
wapi psk wlan0 <WPA2_PASSWORD> 3
wapi essid wlan0 <SSID> 1
renew wlan0
ifconfig wlan0
ping -I wlan0 -c 4 <ROUTER_IPV4>
wapi show wlan0
wapi disconnect wlan0
```

`wapi scan wlan0` starts an active scan and immediately retrieves results. Mode `2` is STA, PSK algorithm `3` is CCMP. Use a numeric router address for `ping` because DNS support is not established by this defconfig. No files were edited.
